roles.failed: Cannot read the role table. The eight preset roles are built in, so this means the backend is down or unconfigured — not that there are no roles.
roles.footnote: The eight roles ship with the app. Roles are defined first and bound to a runtime after: moving a role to the other end does not change the state machine, and one runtime can serve several roles.
roles.note.acpBody: Runtime = which adapter process to launch · Session mode = session/set_config_option (values come from the configOptions returned by session/new; the older session/set_mode is only a fallback) · Permission policy = how the client answers session/request_permission · Prompts and skills = each turn's prompt and the injected roots.
roles.note.acpTitle: What these settings map to in ACP
roles.note.notProvidedBody: Model and reasoning effort are not part of the protocol — each runtime decides them through its own config (claude's settings, codex's config). The app only records which runtime version and mode were actually used, and writes that into the execution report.
